The main takeaway from our work is that

a dynamic procedure for DDES is indeed possible, but the implementation is more complicated than for a dynamic procedure for RANS, due to the presence of an eddy viscosity in the model constant expression, and to the need for a correction for the log-law mismatch.

the dynamic procedure is able to compute the model constant Cdes in a manner that is consistent with the original DDES formulation, and that the dynamic procedure can also be applied in the context of the recent alternate formulation.

the dynamic procedure is effective in capturing the correct behavior of the model constant, as it is able to reproduce a constant value for the model constant in regions where the flow is fully turbulent, and it is able to produce a model constant that varies smoothly with distance to the wall in regions where the eddies are of comparable scale to the grid spacing, i.e., in the near-wall region.
